learner_visual_status.note: Manual photo-led card enrichment with one pixel-reviewed exact-source original image, 4-taxon genus comparison, diagnostic photo checklist. Unshown anatomy and nativity hold preserved.

best_field_traits: Basal winter rosette of shorter, broader blades; spring flowering culms and autumn secondary branches can look dramatically different.
Open spring panicle commonly about 4–13 cm long; later branch heads can be small and partly sheathed.
Lance-shaped stem blades often 3–14 cm long and 3–12 mm wide.
Ligule fringe of hairs about 1–4.2 mm long in broad treatments.
Sheaths range from nearly smooth to coarse hairy, sometimes with raised tubercle/pustule bases; avoid identifying from sheath hair alone.
Mature spikelets commonly 2.9–4 mm; lower glume is shorter than entire spikelet.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Winter rosette / whole rooted tuft, followed by same clump spring full panicle
Three ripe spikelets 2.9–4 mm under calibrated scale and separate glumes
Blade/sheath ligule 1–4 mm fringe with mm reference, showing actual collar versus leaf-base cilia
Leaf sheath hairs and swollen hair bases photographed with accurate side-light

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with D. lindheimeri, ripe spikelets are much larger (~2.9–4 vs 1.3–1.6 mm); compared with D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm), lengths overlap and true collar fringe plus leaf widths are critical. D. commutatum may have broad/cordate stem blade bases and minute/absent true ligule. Don't force the identity from one branching inflorescence.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.look_here_first: Look for a rooted perennial with basal rosette and an open spring panicle; confirm with mature oval spikelets and true ligule.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.measured_diagnostic: Published subsp. oligosanthes treatment: spikelets approximately 2.9–3.9 mm, lower glume 1–1.8 mm, hair-fringe ligule 1–3 mm. These figures do not independently confirm subspecies identity for the canonical card.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.local_lookalikes: D. lindheimeri usually smaller-spikeleted; D. pedicellatum overlaps, so inspect ligule and blade base; D. commutatum may have broader blade bases.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Matched rosette and flowering culm, three measured spikelets, detached glumes/sterile lemma, sheath hairs and true ligule with mm scale.
